question: Should `/set/geolocation` intentionally return HTTP 400 for malformed or non-HTTP(S) explicit origins instead of preserving the prior partial-success response?
rationale: The stricter behavior is technically correct and prevents partial mutation, but it is a user-visible request-contract change that maintainers should accept explicitly.

options.title: Accept strict validation
options.body: Return HTTP 400 before mutation because an invalid explicit origin cannot complete the requested geolocation-plus-permission operation correctly.

options.title: Preserve permissive behavior
options.body: Retain the old response behavior, accepting that malformed origins can produce partially applied state without the requested permission.

recommendation.title: Accept strict validation
recommendation.body: Return HTTP 400 before mutation because an invalid explicit origin cannot complete the requested geolocation-plus-permission operation correctly.
